about: The rule each leveling route is worked out by (lib/guide.mjs RULES; was: the rule the route had in 1.0.6 as released, static/route-release.json, which gives the released route again; was+stay: that rule with the stays across the sea of `stay` laid over it; Rep: with the quests that ask for a standing kills lead to, Desolace’s Gelkis, and the way they open into Shen’dralas; stayHalf: stays only rather than grind half a level; stay2: stays only for two levels of quests across the sea). Chosen on November 15, 2026 with `routes.mjs --choose`: every route was tried by all eight rules of ROUTE_RULES (six where the route’s released rule is the corrected plan alone, for which was+stay is stay), each held to the gate of lib/guide.mjs (no more hours than in 1.0.6 as released, fewer levels ground, no more of them in a row unless it grinds as much less in all, at most three more short visits and one more for every level no longer ground, never over 20 changes of continent unless the route is both faster and grinds less). The choice was made in passes: of the first four rules, the one that grinds least; then, for a route none of those passed for, of the four careful ones, the one that grinds least; and in the last pass a route changed only where a rule passed the gate and beat its choice on levels ground without taking more hours than it. A rebuild works each route out by its rule here, and by its released rule if that one no longer passes the gate. (The Skyborne’s island routes have no rule: they keep the released rules to level 12.) On November 18, 2026, on QuestieDB 1.1.3 (traces of November 17), eight routes that no longer met the gate by their rule were chosen again the same way: human-warrior, human-paladin, human-hunter, human-priest, night-elf-hunter, night-elf-rogue, orc-warrior, troll-warrior.
